pages: Welcome, traveler!
You've just stepped into Reza's world.
Reza is a Computer Engineer and Unity Developer — a sharp-eyed ISTJ who reads patterns like a detective and logs bugs like a bounty hunter.
He builds games in C#, crafts backends with Python & Django, and ships Telegram bots.
Right now, he's leveling up in Machine Learning.
Explore the world to uncover his projects, experiments, and skills. Every path leads somewhere different in his journey.
Take your time. There's a lot to discover!
Want to get in touch, or see the work behind the world?
Pick a link below — click it, tap it, or press its number key.
Where's Reza? Oh, you came looking for him too?
Good luck with that.
He's probably hiding from sunlight, building something nobody asked for, or fixing a bug he definitely created himself.
Anyway, I'm Sajjad. Reza's best friend.
We've known each other since high school.
We went to different universities to study Computer Engineering, but that didn't stop us from spending half our lives on Telegram.
Different campuses. Same nonsense.
Honestly, I've probably talked to Reza more than some people talk to their actual roommates.
University stress, stupid ideas, broken code... we've shared it all.
He's been building things for years.
Games, websites, bots, machine learning...
I still can't tell if he enjoys programming or is just incapable of leaving a problem unsolved. Probably both.
By the way, I helped with this world.
No, I didn't design anything. But I was there.
Emotional support, questionable suggestions, occasional distractions. Essential to any development team.
Reza's an ISTJ, by the way.
The kind of guy who checks everything twice and probably has a backup plan for his backup plan.
I prefer to discover problems organically.
He's twenty-five, with a 16.5 GPA, a GitHub full of projects, and a few unfinished plans.
He still hasn't dealt with his military service, though. But hey, nobody's perfect.
Especially developers. They can build an entire world and still forget to take a break.
Now, if you'll excuse me, I think I hear him arguing with his compiler again.
Wait... you're still here?
I've told you everything I know about Reza. Well, everything I'm legally allowed to share.
Some things stay between best friends.
Anyway, go explore!
There's a whole world out there, and I'm sure Reza spent an unreasonable amount of time on every little detail.
I'll be here.
Someone has to supervise this place while he's busy debugging.
Grrr... oh! A visitor!
Welcome, little human.
Don't worry, I'm friendly.
Well, mostly.
I did accidentally scare away three travelers this morning. Apparently, roaring isn't a proper greeting.
Before you ask: yes, I'm a bear. Yes, I can talk.
And no, I don't eat visitors. I have standards.
Besides, Sajjad's snacks are much easier to steal.
See this flag I'm carrying? It's the Lion and Sun, an old emblem of Persia.
A lion, a sword, a rising sun. I'm no lion, but someone has to watch the sun around here.
I've heard quite a bit about Reza.
He builds games, develops software, creates bots, and experiments with machine learning. Quite ambitious for one human.
I asked him when he planned to rest.
He said, 'After I finish this.'
I asked what 'this' was.
He said, 'Everything.'
...I still don't understand humans.
You know, I like this place. A warm fire, a quiet evening, and a world full of things waiting to be discovered.
It reminds me of something important: you don't have to know where every path leads.
Sometimes the best adventures begin when you simply start walking.
Just watch where you step. I once walked into a tree.
It was a very stubborn tree.
Ah, you've heard all my stories.
I hope you enjoyed them. I'd tell you more, but even bears need to save some stories for another day.
Go on, little adventurer.
There are still paths to explore and secrets to uncover.
I'll stay here and guard the fire. And the flag.
